text:
jane.doe: Hey, hitting a 400 when calling tool `pdf_extractor` — error says: JSON parse error: invalid character 0x08 at offset 27. Copy of the JSON body I sent:

```json
{
  "file_path": "C:\Users\Jane\documents\notes.txt",
  "comment": "Summary:\bContains sensitive lines that I pasted",
  "options": {}
}
```

It works locally for me in the SDK, but the hosted API rejects it. Any ideas?

amy_support: Thanks — can you confirm whether you pasted from a Windows editor or a word processor? That error (0x08) usually means a literal backspace/control-B in the string. Are you using our JS SDK, curl, or the web playground? Also please paste the request_id from the error if present.

jane.doe: Using our internal node SDK (v1.3.2). Error returned with request_id `req_0a1b2c3d`. I pasted the comment from an exported .txt. I tried escaping in the client as `\b` and it still failed initially.

infra-bot: logged: request=req_0a1b2c3d parse_error=invalid_character offset=27 char=0x08 (BACKSPACE) service=tools-parse node=tools-prod-07

ron_eng: This matches a literal control char in the request body. Some editors insert a backspace or special control char when cleaning formatting; JSON parsers will choke if the actual 0x08 byte is present instead of the escape sequence \b. Quick checks/repro:
- In Node: `Buffer.from(body).includes(0x08)` will show it.
- Or run: `cat payload.json | sed -n l` to visualize hidden chars.

ron_eng: Workarounds:
1) Sanitize client-side: strip control chars before sending: `body.comment = body.comment.replace(/[\x00-\x1F]/g, "");` (if acceptable).
2) Properly escape backspace: replace literal with `\b`: `body.comment = body.comment.replace(/\x08/g, "\\b");`
3) As a safe transport, Base64-encode the problematic field and decode server-side: `comment_b64` — avoids parser issues entirely.

amy_support: Minimal curl repro (shows the problem):

```bash
echo -e '{"comment":"Line1\bLine2"}' | curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/exec \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @-
# this will show 400 if the echo inserts an actual backspace byte
```

amy_support: Quick fix you can try: in JS ensure you escape with `JSON.stringify` (it will turn backspace into `\b`) or explicitly replace `\u0008` with `\b` before sending.

jane.doe: Thanks — I ran `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).includes(0x08)` and it returned false, then `Buffer.from(payload.comment)` returned true — turns out our paste included a literal backspace. Replaced with `\b` and the API accepted the request. All good now, appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

ron_eng: Glad it helped — we'll add a short troubleshooting blurb to the docs about hidden control chars in tool args (and a diagnostic snippet).
